pattern.crimePattern: a private banker taking commission on the account behind the Mvua till pushes the analyst who traced it down the fire stairs, after luring her there with a fake "lifts out of service" notice
pattern.notes: Fictional bank, trust and staff. Region 10, case 1: closes t_mvua as traced (three-headed). Introduces Anjali Mehta, head of compliance, as an ally. The fake notice frames a story (an accident), not a person.

ob.text: A bank in the CBD reports a member of staff, financial-crime analyst Nasimiyu Wekesa (34), found dead on its internal fire stairs on Monday night. The bank's first report says she fell while the lifts were out of service.

facts.text: Nasimiyu Wekesa was found dead on Jumuiya Bank's internal fire stairs on Monday night; the bank says she fell while the lifts were out of service.
Fall injuries on the landing between 16 and 17. Her bag is open; there is no case file in it.
Omari: at about twenty to ten he heard a cry in the stairwell above 14, then a door upstairs; he ran up and found her at quarter to ten. His radio log: 21:46.
Omari: the lift lobbies have cameras; the stairwells don't.
Lobby camera: Omari on floor 14 until he ran up at 21:41.
Beside the floor-18 lifts: "LIFTS OUT OF SERVICE 21:00–23:00. PLEASE USE THE STAIRS. — Facilities."
Nasimiyu's laptop is still on her desk.
Facilities log: no lift maintenance on Monday. The lifts' own logs show them working all night.
Nasimiyu to Anjali, 21:05: "Escalating. Till 880 214 settles into Msingi Trust. RM: M. Salim. I'm filing an STR in the morning." Two earlier escalations to Gideon went unanswered.
Anjali: Nasimiyu carried her case file home every night. Her ex-fiancé Kelvin used to tease her about it.
The Msingi settlement account paid "S. Kiprop, Advocate — retainer" and "Mlinzi Bora Security — KSh 2,000,000".
The Msingi Trust has three nominee directors: Okoth Oduya, Mary Chepkemoi and Advocate Wanjiru Nderitu.
Print log: the notice was printed at 21:12 on the floor-15 printer from workstation PB-07, user msalim.
Badge log: 21:19 floor-18 door "held open"; 21:38 Nasimiyu into the stairwell from 18; 21:44 Mwanaisha out of the stairwell onto 15, with no swipe in between.
Every staff member swipes onto floor 18; a "door held open" alert means someone was let in without a swipe.
Gideon forwarded both escalations to the Msingi file with the note "Hold, large client". His badge went out at 19:00.
Gideon's family and his car tracker: home in Kitengela from 20:00.
Her desk calendar and a café receipt: lunch with "K." on Monday; café staff say Kelvin and Nasimiyu argued about the wedding being off.
Kelvin was at the football at Kasarani 20:00–22:30 (ticket, photos).
Sylvia's flatmates: she was home from 18:30.
Anjali was at a dinner in Gigiri until 23:00.
Records: at 21:58 Mwanaisha called the number Mlinzi Bora's office used (case 90), now disconnected.
Records: a monthly "commission" into Mwanaisha's account from Till 880 214, for four years.
In Mwanaisha's laundry bag: Nasimiyu's case file.
In her flat: a roll of clear tape like the one on the notice.
Fingerprints taken from Mwanaisha in detention.
Post-mortem: head and neck injuries from a fall down a flight, and grip bruises on both upper arms made just before.
Post-mortem: death on Monday between 21:38 and 21:46.
Lab: Mwanaisha's prints on the back of the notice and on the tape roll.
Lab: fibres under Nasimiyu's fingernails match Mwanaisha's jacket.
Missing: there's no case file in her bag.
Missing: there's no camera in the stairwell.
Missing: there's no swipe for the visitor at 21:19.
Missing: Gideon never answered her escalations.
Missing: there's no lift maintenance in the facilities log.

Mwanaisha: "Msingi Trust is a clean client."
Mwanaisha: "Four years of commission. Enough to put my children through university abroad. She was going to file in the morning. I asked her for one week."

reconstruction.text: For six weeks Nasimiyu traces the account where Till 880 214 settles its takings. It leads to the Msingi Trust, run by Mwanaisha, who has taken a private commission from it for four years. Gideon sits on two escalations.

Monday, 21:05: she emails Anjali over his head and says she'll file in the morning. At 21:12 Mwanaisha prints "LIFTS OUT OF SERVICE" on the floor-15 printer. At 21:19 she knocks on 18's glass door; Nasimiyu lets her in and refuses to wait a week.

Mwanaisha tapes the notice by the lifts and waits on the landing between 17 and 16. At 21:38 Nasimiyu takes the stairs. Mwanaisha grabs her case file; Nasimiyu pulls it back; Mwanaisha shoves her headfirst down the flight.
She takes the file, goes down to 15 and swipes out of the stairwell at 21:44. At 21:46 Omari radios it in. At 21:58 Mwanaisha calls a number that used to ring at Mlinzi Bora.

afterVerdict.beat: Anjali Mehta hands Amani the Msingi Trust's full file, signed over to the ODPP. "Everything. I should have read her email on Monday."
The trust's three nominee directors each lead somewhere.

files.text: Traced: three-headed. Msingi's directors lead to Okoth Oduya (Raphael Oduya's nephew), Mary Chepkemoi (company secretary of Stanley Rotich's firm) and Advocate Wanjiru Nderitu (legal officer of Margaret Kabiru's Ukarimu Foundation).

afterVerdict.beat: Halima, reading it: "They built it so each of them could point at the other two." Amani's notebook: "Three directors, three names. Of course. Nobody holds the knife alone."

clockPlan.note: Two stamps: records on Mwanaisha and a warrant on her flat. Detain her after the search; the prints (6 h) and fibres (12 h) come back inside 24 h.
